verdict.reasoning: Transcript supports 3‑day history, watery diarrhea, about hourly, and no blood, but does not mention that stools disturb or wake from sleep. Patient says, “I feel like it's like almost every hour I'm awake,” implying episodes while awake, not during sleep.
As above, transcript supports 3‑day watery diarrhea about hourly with no blood, but there is no statement that it wakes the patient from sleep; instead, “almost every hour I'm awake.”

Crampy lower central abdominal pain is described: “It's like at the bottom… feels pretty like in the middle to me,” and rated about 6–7/10: patient suggests “maybe is that like a six or seven?” The transcript doesn’t use the term periumbilical but central lower abdominal is a reasonable clinical synonym.

Patient reports nausea and vomiting, particularly with milk: “I definitely feel kind of nauseous… I have vomited… whenever I have, like, milk… I just feel like I want to vomit. And actually… had some milk and I just completely vomited it.”
Patient feels hot/feverish with no measured temperature: “I think I am pretty. I feel kind of really hot all the time… I haven't actually done any temperature reading or anything like that.”
Decreased frequency but still passing urine is stated: “Are you passing urine? Okay.” Patient: “Yeah, but I guess less frequently maybe, but it seems to be okay.”
Brother with similar illness now improving: “my, my brother has had, actually had something like this… for five days as well… I think he's getting better, but I'm not really sure.”
Patient denies other medical history: “I think otherwise I'm fit. Well… I can't think of any related medical history… no, I don't think so.”
Recent paracetamol use: “I've been taking some, like, paracetamols and stuff like that lately, but… I'm not on any regular medication.”

Plan to continue paracetamol PRN: “You can try just, you know, regular paracetamol if you are feeling feverish,” and later, “If you've got bit of tummy pain, if you're feeling feverish, then I think paracetamol is very sensible.”
No known drug allergies: “do you have any allergies to any medications?” Patient: “I don't have any allergies that I know of.”

Father has colon cancer described as third stage: “My dad actually has colon cancer at the moment… he's sort of in his third stage. I'm not sure what that means exactly.” Stage III is a direct restatement of ‘third stage.’
Living situation: “I live with my um, sister and my mum.”
Work role and location: “I work at an office in central London. It's. So I work in government.”
Eating separately from household: “I just haven't really… I don't normally actually eat with my family. I normally, I'm buying stuff and that kind of thing.”
Social smoking mainly Fridays: “I smoke for like socially but not like regularly. So normally if it's a Friday or something like that, I might have a cigarette.”
Binge‑type alcohol use 1–2x/month: “Maybe on Fridays I have more alcohol but yeah… I suppose not every week but maybe once or twice a month that… I'll go out with my friends and we'll drink a lot.”

Doctor’s assessment of gastroenteritis is supported (“symptoms are suggestive of something called gastroenteritis… I suspect this will just settle down… just like it did for your brother”), as are 3‑day watery diarrhea, nausea/vomiting, feeling hot, and sick contact. However, the transcript does not explicitly state ‘no red flags on history’ or ‘likely viral in etiology’; those are new interpretive additions beyond what is said.

Oral rehydration with over‑the‑counter Dioralyte: “you can get things like diurelite, which is a fluid replacement we can get from the pharmacy. It's probably worth recommending that.” Also: “No, you can just get over the counter.”

Clear fluids and soft diet: “So clear fluids you can use soft diet, things like soup, mash, and then gradually build up as much as your body can tolerate. But really, let's try and keep yourself well hydrated first.”

Advice to continue paracetamol PRN: “You can try just, you know, regular paracetamol if you are feeling feverish,” and, when asked if it’s okay to carry on, “Absolutely… then I think paracetamol is very sensible.”
Advice to avoid alcohol: “Try and avoid alcohol if you can.”

Safety‑net about 48 hours and dehydration: “if your symptoms aren't settling down in the next couple of days, so 48 hours, I want you to give me a call back because… if you are getting dehydrated, then we need to do further investigations.”

Follow‑up advice matches safety‑net: “if your symptoms aren't settling down in the next couple of days, so 48 hours, I want you to give me a call back… if you are getting dehydrated, then we need to do further investigations.”
No physical examination is described anywhere in the transcript; thus, stating that no objective physical exam findings were documented is consistent with the record.
